title: Design an explanatory interactive quiz
description: Write clear questions, plausible distractors and explanations linked to the objective.
accomplishes: Write clear questions, plausible distractors and explanations linked to the objective. Avoid trick wording and unsupported facts. Define feedback and retry behaviour, marking any question that needs source verification rather than presenting a quiz as a complete assessment.
prompt:
Act as an instructional designer.

Task: Design an explanatory interactive quiz.

Input context:
- TOPIC: [TOPIC]
- LEVEL: [LEVEL]
- OBJECTIVE: [OBJECTIVE]
- FORMAT: [FORMAT]

Write clear questions, plausible distractors and explanations linked to the objective. Avoid trick wording and unsupported facts. Define feedback and retry behaviour, marking any question that needs source verification rather than presenting a quiz as a complete assessment.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Data-quality quiz
Ask which action preserves leading zeros in identifiers, then explain why treating identifiers as ordinary numbers can be wrong. A distractor should reflect a real misconception, not random wording. Offer a short follow-up example after feedback. Review answers against the source before use; no learner score or question validity is established here.
